content.text:
Map each node in every diagram on the provided canvas to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change any diagram’s text or the canvas layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (terminal):
Map all nodes of d5 only. Read numbered ranges and full named declarations, cover flows. Return JSON.

   330	/// Initialize a new terminal with the given options.
   331	///
   332	/// The returned terminal owns its memory. Call `deinit` with the same
   333	/// allocator when you are done with it.
   334	///
   335	/// ```zig
   336	/// var t: Terminal = try .init(io, alloc, .{ .cols = 80, .rows = 24 });
   337	/// defer t.deinit(alloc);
   338	/// ```
   339	///
   340	/// Returns `error.InvalidValue` if `cols` or `rows` is zero. This check
   341	/// happens before anything is allocated. If the size comes from an
   342	/// untrusted source, you can rely on this check instead of validating
   343	/// it yourself.
   344	pub fn init(
   345	    io_impl: std.Io,
   346	    alloc: Allocator,
   347	    opts: Options,
   348	) !Terminal {
   349	    const cols = opts.cols;
   350	    const rows = opts.rows;
   351	
   352	    // The screens and scrolling region need at least one row and column.
   353	    // Check this before allocating so there is nothing to clean up.
   354	    if (cols == 0 or rows == 0) return error.InvalidValue;
   355	
   356	    var screen_set: ScreenSet = try .init(io_impl, alloc, .{
   357	        .cols = cols,
   358	        .rows = rows,
   359	        .max_scrollback_bytes = opts.max_scrollback_bytes,
   360	        .max_scrollback_lines = opts.max_scrollback_lines,
   361	        .kitty_image_storage_limit = opts.kitty_image_storage_limit,
   362	        .kitty_image_loading_limits = opts.kitty_image_loading_limits,
   363	    });
   364	    errdefer screen_set.deinit(alloc);
   365	
   366	    var result: Terminal = .{
   367	        .cols = cols,
   368	        .rows = rows,
   369	        .screens = screen_set,
   370	        .tabstops = try .init(alloc, cols, TABSTOP_INTERVAL),
   371	        .scrolling_region = .{
   372	            .top = 0,
   373	            .bottom = rows - 1,
   374	            .left = 0,
   375	            .right = cols - 1,
   376	        },
   377	        .pwd = .empty,
   378	        .title = .empty,
   379	        .colors = opts.colors,
   380	        .modes = .{
   381	            .values = opts.default_modes,
   382	            .default = opts.default_modes,
   383	        },
   384	        .cursor = .{
   385	            .default_style = opts.default_cursor_style,
   386	            .default_blink = opts.default_cursor_blink,
   387	        },
   388	        .default_xt_checksum = opts.default_xt_checksum,
   389	    };
   390	    result.flags.xt_checksum = opts.default_xt_checksum;
   391	    result.setCursorStyle(.default);
   392	    return result;
   393	}

   308	/// Initialize a new screen.
   309	///
   310	/// max_scrollback_bytes is the amount of scrollback to keep in bytes. This
   311	/// will be rounded UP to the nearest page size because our minimum allocation
   312	/// size is that anyways.
   313	///
   314	/// If max scrollback is 0, then no scrollback is kept at all.
   315	pub fn init(
   316	    io: std.Io,
   317	    alloc: Allocator,
   318	    opts: Options,
   319	) Allocator.Error!Screen {
   320	    // Initialize our backing pages.
   321	    var pages = try PageList.init(alloc, .{
   322	        .cols = opts.cols,
   323	        .rows = opts.rows,
   324	        .max_size = opts.max_scrollback_bytes,
   325	        .max_lines = opts.max_scrollback_lines,
   326	    });
   327	    errdefer pages.deinit();
   328	
   329	    // Create our tracked pin for the cursor.
   330	    const page_pin = try pages.trackPin(.{ .node = pages.pages.first.? });
   331	    errdefer pages.untrackPin(page_pin);
   332	    const page_rac = page_pin.rowAndCell();
   333	
   334	    var result: Screen = .{
   335	        .io = io,
   336	        .alloc = alloc,
   337	        .pages = pages,
   338	        .no_scrollback = opts.max_scrollback_bytes == 0,
   339	        .cursor = .{
   340	            .x = 0,
   341	            .y = 0,
   342	            .page_pin = page_pin,
   343	            .page_row = page_rac.row,
   344	            .page_cell = page_rac.cell,
   345	        },
   346	    };
   347	
   348	    if (comptime build_options.kitty_graphics) {
   349	        result.kitty_images.setLimit(
   350	            io,
   351	            alloc,
   352	            &result,
   353	            opts.kitty_image_storage_limit,
   354	        );
   355	        result.kitty_images.image_limits = opts.kitty_image_loading_limits;
   356	    }
   357	
   358	    return result;
   359	}

   366	    self.pages.deinit();

   308	/// Initialize a new screen.
   309	///
   310	/// max_scrollback_bytes is the amount of scrollback to keep in bytes. This
   311	/// will be rounded UP to the nearest page size because our minimum allocation
   312	/// size is that anyways.
   313	///
   314	/// If max scrollback is 0, then no scrollback is kept at all.
   315	pub fn init(
   316	    io: std.Io,
   317	    alloc: Allocator,
   318	    opts: Options,
   319	) Allocator.Error!Screen {
   320	    // Initialize our backing pages.
   321	    var pages = try PageList.init(alloc, .{
   322	        .cols = opts.cols,
   323	        .rows = opts.rows,
   324	        .max_size = opts.max_scrollback_bytes,
   325	        .max_lines = opts.max_scrollback_lines,
   326	    });
   327	    errdefer pages.deinit();
   328	
   329	    // Create our tracked pin for the cursor.
   330	    const page_pin = try pages.trackPin(.{ .node = pages.pages.first.? });
   331	    errdefer pages.untrackPin(page_pin);
   332	    const page_rac = page_pin.rowAndCell();
   333	
   334	    var result: Screen = .{
   335	        .io = io,
   336	        .alloc = alloc,
   337	        .pages = pages,
   338	        .no_scrollback = opts.max_scrollback_bytes == 0,
   339	        .cursor = .{
   340	            .x = 0,
   341	            .y = 0,
   342	            .page_pin = page_pin,
   343	            .page_row = page_rac.row,
   344	            .page_cell = page_rac.cell,
   345	        },
   346	    };
   347	
   348	    if (comptime build_options.kitty_graphics) {
   349	        result.kitty_images.setLimit(
   350	            io,
   351	            alloc,
   352	            &result,
   353	            opts.kitty_image_storage_limit,
   354	        );
   355	        result.kitty_images.image_limits = opts.kitty_image_loading_limits;
   356	    }
   357	
   358	    return result;
   359	}

   330	/// Initialize a new terminal with the given options.
   331	///
   332	/// The returned terminal owns its memory. Call `deinit` with the same
   333	/// allocator when you are done with it.
   334	///
   335	/// ```zig
   336	/// var t: Terminal = try .init(io, alloc, .{ .cols = 80, .rows = 24 });
   337	/// defer t.deinit(alloc);
   338	/// ```
   339	///
   340	/// Returns `error.InvalidValue` if `cols` or `rows` is zero. This check
   341	/// happens before anything is allocated. If the size comes from an
   342	/// untrusted source, you can rely on this check instead of validating
   343	/// it yourself.
   344	pub fn init(
   345	    io_impl: std.Io,
   346	    alloc: Allocator,
   347	    opts: Options,
   348	) !Terminal {
   349	    const cols = opts.cols;
   350	    const rows = opts.rows;
   351	
   352	    // The screens and scrolling region need at least one row and column.
   353	    // Check this before allocating so there is nothing to clean up.
   354	    if (cols == 0 or rows == 0) return error.InvalidValue;
   355	
   356	    var screen_set: ScreenSet = try .init(io_impl, alloc, .{
   357	        .cols = cols,
   358	        .rows = rows,
   359	        .max_scrollback_bytes = opts.max_scrollback_bytes,
   360	        .max_scrollback_lines = opts.max_scrollback_lines,
   361	        .kitty_image_storage_limit = opts.kitty_image_storage_limit,
   362	        .kitty_image_loading_limits = opts.kitty_image_loading_limits,
   363	    });
   364	    errdefer screen_set.deinit(alloc);
   365	
   366	    var result: Terminal = .{
   367	        .cols = cols,
   368	        .rows = rows,
   369	        .screens = screen_set,
   370	        .tabstops = try .init(alloc, cols, TABSTOP_INTERVAL),
   371	        .scrolling_region = .{
   372	            .top = 0,
   373	            .bottom = rows - 1,
   374	            .left = 0,
   375	            .right = cols - 1,
   376	        },
   377	        .pwd = .empty,
   378	        .title = .empty,
   379	        .colors = opts.colors,
   380	        .modes = .{
   381	            .values = opts.default_modes,
   382	            .default = opts.default_modes,
   383	        },
   384	        .cursor = .{
   385	            .default_style = opts.default_cursor_style,
   386	            .default_blink = opts.default_cursor_blink,
   387	        },
   388	        .default_xt_checksum = opts.default_xt_checksum,
   389	    };

   310	/// max_scrollback_bytes is the amount of scrollback to keep in bytes. This
   311	/// will be rounded UP to the nearest page size because our minimum allocation

   322	        .cols = opts.cols,

   324	        .max_size = opts.max_scrollback_bytes,

   329	    // Create our tracked pin for the cursor.

   335	        .io = io,
   336	        .alloc = alloc,
   337	        .pages = pages,
   338	        .no_scrollback = opts.max_scrollback_bytes == 0,
   339	        .cursor = .{
   340	            .x = 0,
   341	            .y = 0,
   342	            .page_pin = page_pin,
   343	            .page_row = page_rac.row,
   344	            .page_cell = page_rac.cell,
   345	        },
   346	    };

   348	    if (comptime build_options.kitty_graphics) {
   349	        result.kitty_images.setLimit(
   350	            io,
   351	            alloc,
   352	            &result,
   353	            opts.kitty_image_storage_limit,
   354	        );

   356	    }

   308	/// Initialize a new screen.
   309	///
   310	/// max_scrollback_bytes is the amount of scrollback to keep in bytes. This
   311	/// will be rounded UP to the nearest page size because our minimum allocation
   312	/// size is that anyways.
   313	///
   314	/// If max scrollback is 0, then no scrollback is kept at all.
   315	pub fn init(
   316	    io: std.Io,
   317	    alloc: Allocator,
   318	    opts: Options,
   319	) Allocator.Error!Screen {
   320	    // Initialize our backing pages.
   321	    var pages = try PageList.init(alloc, .{
   322	        .cols = opts.cols,
   323	        .rows = opts.rows,
   324	        .max_size = opts.max_scrollback_bytes,
   325	        .max_lines = opts.max_scrollback_lines,
   326	    });
   327	    errdefer pages.deinit();
   328	
   329	    // Create our tracked pin for the cursor.
   330	    const page_pin = try pages.trackPin(.{ .node = pages.pages.first.? });
   331	    errdefer pages.untrackPin(page_pin);
   332	    const page_rac = page_pin.rowAndCell();
   333	
   334	    var result: Screen = .{
   335	        .io = io,
   336	        .alloc = alloc,
   337	        .pages = pages,
   338	        .no_scrollback = opts.max_scrollback_bytes == 0,
   339	        .cursor = .{
   340	            .x = 0,
   341	            .y = 0,
   342	            .page_pin = page_pin,
   343	            .page_row = page_rac.row,
   344	            .page_cell = page_rac.cell,
   345	        },
   346	    };
   347	
   348	    if (comptime build_options.kitty_graphics) {
   349	        result.kitty_images.setLimit(
   350	            io,
   351	            alloc,
   352	            &result,
   353	            opts.kitty_image_storage_limit,
   354	        );
   355	        result.kitty_images.image_limits = opts.kitty_image_loading_limits;
   356	    }
   357	
   358	    return result;
   359	}

   352	    // The screens and scrolling region need at least one row and column.

   362	        .kitty_image_loading_limits = opts.kitty_image_loading_limits,

    35	/// The number of pages we preheat the page pool with. For operating systems
    36	/// that support it, pages are demand-paged (see PagePool) so this only
    37	/// costs us address space. For other operating systems, we don't preheat.
    38	const page_preheat = 4;
    39	
    40	/// The number of nodes we preheat the node pool with. Unlike pages, nodes
    41	/// are ordinary heap memory so every idle preheated node costs real
    42	/// memory. A new PageList needs exactly one node for its first page, so
    43	/// we preheat that one and let the pool grow on demand.
    44	const node_preheat = 1;
    45	
    46	/// The number of pins we preheat the pin pool with: the viewport pin that
    47	/// every PageList tracks and the cursor pin that every Screen tracks.
    48	/// Selections, searches, and so on grow the pool on demand.
    49	const pin_preheat = 2;
    50	
    51	/// The list of pages in the screen. These are expected to be in order
    52	/// where the first page is the topmost page (scrollback) and the last is
    53	/// the bottommost page (the current active page).
    54	pub const List = DoublyLinkedList(Node);
    55	
    56	/// A single node within the PageList linked list.
    57	///
    58	/// This isn't pub because you can access the type via List.Node.
    59	const Node = struct {
    60	    prev: ?*Node = null,
    61	    next: ?*Node = null,
    62	    data: Data,
    63	    serial: u64,
    64	
    65	    /// How the backing memory of the embedded Page was allocated. Pool-owned
    66	    /// memory is always a full standard-size item from the memory
    67	    /// pool, regardless of the page layout size. Heap-owned memory
    68	    /// is allocated directly with the page allocator and is exactly
    69	    /// `Page.memory.len` bytes.
    70	    ///
    71	    /// This must never be inferred from the memory length: heap-owned
    72	    /// pages can be smaller than the standard size (e.g. compacted
    73	    /// pages), and returning one to the pool would corrupt it.
    74	    ///
    75	    /// This has no default on purpose so that every construction site
    76	    /// is forced to make an explicit decision.
    77	    owned: Owned,
    78	
    79	    /// The physical representation of the page contents.
    80	    ///
    81	    /// Both states retain the same `Page.memory` virtual mapping and the same
    82	    /// `Page` metadata. A resident page can access the mapping directly since
    83	    /// it is, well, resident.
    84	    ///
    85	    /// A compressed page owns an encoded copy while the physical memory
    86	    /// behind the raw mapping is discarded. HOWEVER, we retain the
    87	    /// virtual allocation so that restoration is infallible.
    88	    const Data = union(enum) {
    89	        resident: Page,
    90	        compressed: compression.Page,
    91	    };
    92	
    93	    const Owned = enum { pool, heap };
    94	
    95	    /// The backing-memory representation currently stored by this node.
    96	    pub const Storage = enum { resident, compressed };
    97	
    98	    /// Return the terminal page stored in this node.
    99	    ///
   100	    /// WARNING: This will DECOMPRESS compressed pages! Only use this if
   101	    /// you need access to the underlying memory. If you only need access to
   102	    /// metadata (row, col counts etc) then use the other metadata functions.
   103	    pub inline fn page(self: *Node) *Page {
   104	        return switch (self.data) {
   105	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   106	            .compressed => self.restore(.preserve),
   107	        };
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    /// Return the terminal page only when its raw memory is resident.
   111	    ///
   112	    /// Unlike `page`, this never restores a compressed node. This is useful
   113	    /// for diagnostics which can display node metadata without touching the
   114	    /// discarded mapping, but may inspect page contents when they are already
   115	    /// available.
   395	        _ = self.pages.reset(mode);
   396	        _ = self.nodes.reset(mode);
   397	        _ = self.pins.reset(mode);
   398	    }
   399	};

   402	pool: MemoryPool,
   403	
   404	/// The list of pages in the screen.
   405	pages: List,
   406	
   407	/// The next globally unique reference generation for this PageList. A
   408	/// generation is assigned whenever a page is allocated, reused as new, or
   409	/// changed in place such that existing page coordinates are no longer stable.
   410	///
   411	/// The serial number can be used to detect whether the page is identical
   412	/// to the page that was originally referenced by a pointer. Since we reuse
   413	/// and pool memory, pointer stability is not guaranteed, but the serial
   414	/// will always be different for different page generations.
   415	///
   416	/// Developer note: we never do overflow checking on this. If we created
   417	/// a new page every second it'd take 584 billion years to overflow. We're
   418	/// going to risk it.
   419	page_serial: u64,
   420	
   421	/// The first serial in the current whole-list validity epoch. Only `reset`
   422	/// advances this value, immediately before rebuilding every page. It is not
   423	/// the generation of the first page or the exact minimum live generation.
   424	/// Page generations are not monotonic in list order: replacement and split
   425	/// operations can put a fresh generation before older live pages.
   426	///
   427	/// A generation below this epoch is definitely invalid, allowing O(1)
   428	/// rejection in `nodeIsValid` and bulk removal of pre-reset search results.
   429	/// A generation at or above it is only potentially valid and must still be
   430	/// checked against the live list before its coordinates are used.
   431	page_serial_epoch: u64,

   434	/// logical scrollback accounting and does not change while a mapping is
   435	/// decommitted. It excludes encoded storage and unused preheated pool items.
   436	page_size: usize,

  1295	    // become invalid. Rather than do something fancy like we do other
  1296	    // places and try to update it in place, we just invalidate it because
  1297	    // its too easy to get the logic wrong in here.

  1303	        // scrollback even without reflow, which can cross the line limit.
  1304	        self.limits.enforce(self, .lines, .reclaim);
  1305	        return;
  1306	    }

  1309	    // increasing beyond the explicit limits to fit the active area.
  1310	    const old_limits = self.limits;

  1312	        opts.cols orelse self.cols,
  1313	        opts.rows orelse self.rows,

  1318	    // only rows change, reflow is impossible. So we change our behavior based
  1319	    // on the change of columns.
  1320	    const cols = opts.cols orelse self.cols;

content.text:
Map each node in every diagram on the provided canvas to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change any diagram’s text or the canvas layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (terminal):
Map all nodes of d5 only. Read numbered ranges and full named declarations, cover flows. Return JSON.

   330	/// Initialize a new terminal with the given options.
   331	///
   332	/// The returned terminal owns its memory. Call `deinit` with the same
   333	/// allocator when you are done with it.
   334	///
   335	/// ```zig
   336	/// var t: Terminal = try .init(io, alloc, .{ .cols = 80, .rows = 24 });
   337	/// defer t.deinit(alloc);
   338	/// ```
   339	///
   340	/// Returns `error.InvalidValue` if `cols` or `rows` is zero. This check
   341	/// happens before anything is allocated. If the size comes from an
   342	/// untrusted source, you can rely on this check instead of validating
   343	/// it yourself.
   344	pub fn init(
   345	    io_impl: std.Io,
   346	    alloc: Allocator,
   347	    opts: Options,
   348	) !Terminal {
   349	    const cols = opts.cols;
   350	    const rows = opts.rows;
   351	
   352	    // The screens and scrolling region need at least one row and column.
   353	    // Check this before allocating so there is nothing to clean up.
   354	    if (cols == 0 or rows == 0) return error.InvalidValue;
   355	
   356	    var screen_set: ScreenSet = try .init(io_impl, alloc, .{
   357	        .cols = cols,
   358	        .rows = rows,
   359	        .max_scrollback_bytes = opts.max_scrollback_bytes,
   360	        .max_scrollback_lines = opts.max_scrollback_lines,
   361	        .kitty_image_storage_limit = opts.kitty_image_storage_limit,
   362	        .kitty_image_loading_limits = opts.kitty_image_loading_limits,
   363	    });
   364	    errdefer screen_set.deinit(alloc);
   365	
   366	    var result: Terminal = .{
   367	        .cols = cols,
   368	        .rows = rows,
   369	        .screens = screen_set,
   370	        .tabstops = try .init(alloc, cols, TABSTOP_INTERVAL),
   371	        .scrolling_region = .{
   372	            .top = 0,
   373	            .bottom = rows - 1,
   374	            .left = 0,
   375	            .right = cols - 1,
   376	        },
   377	        .pwd = .empty,
   378	        .title = .empty,
   379	        .colors = opts.colors,
   380	        .modes = .{
   381	            .values = opts.default_modes,
   382	            .default = opts.default_modes,
   383	        },
   384	        .cursor = .{
   385	            .default_style = opts.default_cursor_style,
   386	            .default_blink = opts.default_cursor_blink,
   387	        },
   388	        .default_xt_checksum = opts.default_xt_checksum,
   389	    };
   390	    result.flags.xt_checksum = opts.default_xt_checksum;
   391	    result.setCursorStyle(.default);
   392	    return result;
   393	}
